summary: Sequoia National Forest lookout above Lake Isabella, with a 25-foot steel tower by 1942; abandoned after a 1968 fire and now gone.

facts.design: 25-foot steel tower with a house (1942 report)
facts.status_note: The tower is listed as gone; the station was abandoned during a 1968 fire.

visit.trail_note: A graded dirt road goes almost to the top, and the highpoint is a short distance further (trip report).

events.note: Telephone line crew sent to build a line to Cook Peak, where a new lookout was planned
Cliff Harrington and Robert Crain manned the lookout during the June 1942 fire
Fire first spotted by lookouts on Cook Peak; the lookout was encircled and swept by flames, and the tower and house were not damaged
Claude Stewart of Porterville had been a lookout on Cook's Peak for four years
Claude Stewart reported a California condor flying about 100 feet from the lookout station (Fresno Bee)
Mrs. Helen King was the Forest Service lookout on Cook's Peak
Grass and scrub oak fire burned over 980 acres near Lake Isabella and moved up Cook's Peak
Lookout station abandoned during the July 1968 fire; the two newspaper accounts disagree on what burned

corrections.why: firelookout.org lists Cook Peak (Kern, tower gone) at 35.62170 -118.43813, and a trip report puts the Cook Peak summit east of Lake Isabella town. The record point is about 13 km north-west of that. Needs a map check before applying.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Times-Standard says a small cabin, a boat and some sheds were burned at the lookout station; a Fresno paper says the flames skirted the station. The story reports both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: No source gives the build year; the 1936 notice planned it and the 1942 report shows it standing. The 1968 accounts disagree on whether the station building burned. No source gives the date the tower was removed. The record coordinates are about 13 km from firelookout.org's Cook Peak point; the story assumes the trip report's Cook Peak summit is the lookout site, which the firelookout.org point supports. The trip report's 'survey tower remains' and fenced-tower passages describe a different summit (Wyleys Knob) and are not used. Only one newspaper-derived source (the weebly page) carries the 1936-1968 items; the newspaper texts were checked only as quoted on that page, not against the original papers.
